estimate.damage_summary: During an evasive swerve in a car, the laptop was thrown against the car door, cracking its screen and damaging its lower-right corner/housing. The invoice also includes polishing of an old lid scuff and a diagnostic inspection.
estimate.policy_notes: Assuming the schedule has agreed the portable-equipment peril and co-insured household contents, the described impact during the swerve is covered under 2.6.1–2.6.2. Necessary repairs are assessed under 7.1.7 and 7.1.10; pre-existing cosmetic damage is excluded under 7.1.11 and 7.1.8(a). Examination is covered under 5.2.3, subject to its EUR 250 gross per-event cap. No deductible or proportional reduction is specified in the supplied policy text. For the repairs, the estimates are consistent with the stated near-EUR 1,500 combined cost, with most attributable to the display, and remain below the equivalent replacement cost as described.

lines.rationale: The sudden impact and cracked screen are covered areas of damage under 2.6.1–2.6.3, and necessary repair components and labour are included by 7.1.7 and 7.1.10. A complete display assembly is plausible for this repair; the estimate reflects a standard equivalent part and authorised-workshop labour, not an upgrade, and fits the description that the display made up most of the repair cost.

The damaged corner and lower housing are confirmed as damage from the same impact, covered under 2.6.1–2.6.3; replacing the dented shell is a necessary repair under 7.1.7 and 7.1.10. One housing repair is plausible, and the estimated standard replacement shell and labour, together with the display repair, remain consistent with the stated near-EUR 1,500 repair cost and below the equivalent new-unit cost.

lines.invoice_text: Polish of pre-existing lid scuff (surface only, does not affect operation)
lines.rationale: The policy excludes treatment of a pre-existing surface condition that the event did not affect: 7.1.11 and 7.1.8(a) make cosmetic polishing not a repair cost. The line concerns the same laptop but not the reported impact damage, so it is not indemnifiable; the price estimate is stated as if the work were otherwise valid.

The examination needed to establish the extent and scope of repair after an insured portable-equipment event is expressly reimbursable under 5.2.3, subject to the EUR 250 gross per-event cap. One diagnostic inspection is plausible and, as a modest standalone workshop charge, is within that cap; the line is payable only on the assumed insured-event gateway under 2.6.7.
